sam: quick heads-up — ran a perf pass on the host preflight for the canary build and we're seeing host-side overhead spike. tokenization ~= 22% CPU, parse/dispatch ~= 18%. small streaming frames and lots of writev/syscall churn. cc @mia @devin

mia: which canary and region? any flamegraphs or pprof output? :thinking:

sam: canary r1.23 on pool-a (gcp-us-west1). grabbed a short pprof top dump from a 5m run:```
flat  flat%   sum%        cum   cum%   name
45.2s  22.1% 22.1%   45.2s  22.1%  tokenize::scan_bytes
36.8s  18.0% 40.1%   36.8s  18.0%  parse::dispatch_requests
23.1s  11.3% 51.4%   23.1s  11.3%  http2::frame_write_small
15.6s   7.6% 59.0%   15.6s   7.6%  kvcache::evict_walk
```

devin: `http2::frame_write_small` + `writev` noise — we've hit this pattern before. Writev syscall overhead kills CPU when lots of tiny frames. Two quick levers: coalesce small frames on the host proxy (aggregate to ~8k) and adjust kernel selection heuristics for short seq lengths so we use the low-dispatch path.

jules: also seeing kvcache churn correlated with the preparse fragmentation. Preflight is splitting requests into micro-chunks which blow out our eviction walk. Logs show repeated evict on the same shard for a single request id.

luis: repro command? I can run a targeted loadgen.

sam: repro:```
./loadgen --target pool-a --qps 250 --concurrency 64 --seq 32 --payload-pattern micro-chunk
```
I prototyped a tiny coalesce shim: gather tokenized bytes per-request until 512B or EOL before handing to kvcache. Local microbench (100k reqs) shows syscalls -30%, host CPU -6%, p99 tail -9%. No functional regressions in quick smoke.

devin: nice. For kernel selection: current rule picks "vector-kernel" based on avg_seq_len threshold = 64. For short sequences the vector path has dispatch overhead > scalar path. Suggest: compute request histogram and pick kernel per-batch using median_seq_len rather than avg. Cheap change and should reduce dispatch penalty.

mia: sounds reasonable. Risk profile? Any effect on demo users?

devin: small: if we choose scalar kernel more often latency for long sequences could increase slightly, but we can do per-batch heuristic and guard with a feature flag behind canary.

jules: I'll raise telemetry: counters for `kv_evictions_per_request`, `host_writev_calls`, `median_seq_len_per_batch`. Need those to validate in prod.

sam: action items:
- sam: open PR for host coalesce shim (done) -> PR #4219
- devin: kernel-selection change + unit tests, feature-flag it -> WIP branch
- jules: telemetry + dashboards for new counters
- luis: run loadgen on canary pool and paste results here

sam: PR #4219: http://ci.internal/repo/patch/4219 (diff is tiny: coalesce up to 512B, flush on EOL or timer). quick numbers from CI: syscalls/sec down 28%, cpu_seconds down 5.8%, p99 latency down 12% on our microbench.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployed to pool-a at 1777001300, rollout id=rb-2026-03-20-12

luis: kicking loadgen now on pool-a with the same micro-chunk pattern, will post 10m summary in ~12m.

sam: thanks — if loadgen is green we'll keep FF on for 24h and observe telemetry. if any customer-facing regressions revert via rollout console.

mia: please make sure the kernel-selection tweak has a fallback to previous policy if median calc fails or metrics are sparse. Also include an opt-out via env var for enterprise distros.

devin: ack. I'll add a safe fallback and a small litmus test for sequence-edge cases.

sam: rough timeline: PR + tests today, canary deploy tonight, 24h observation. I'll update the rollout thread when loadgen completes.

luis: loadgen results (10m): qps stable, p50 ~ unchanged, p95 -4%, p99 -10%, host_writev_calls -31%, kv_evictions_per_request -40%. Looks promising.

sam: nice work everyone. follow-up: devin please add canary tag `canary/host-coalesce`, jules add dashboards, i'll monitor for 24h then schedule wider rollout. :thumbsup:
